recent_posts.title: Understanding the Meaning of Data Quality for Data Engineers
recent_posts.summary: Data quality is defined by six key dimensions: accuracy, completeness, consistency, timeliness, validity, and uniqueness. Poor data quality can cost organizations 15-25% of revenue through erroneous analytics and missed opportunities. Common challenges include human error, duplicate records, inconsistent formats, and outdated information. Solutions involve continuous monitoring, validation, cleansing, and robust data governance frameworks to maintain trustworthy data assets for decision-making.

recent_posts.title: 4 best practices for improving AI accuracy in data pipelines
recent_posts.summary: Improving AI accuracy in data pipelines requires four key practices: establishing robust data governance frameworks (ownership, stewardship, compliance, dataset catalogs, audits), implementing data quality assurance measures (automated verification, profiling, KPIs, cleaning, feedback loops), utilizing advanced monitoring tools for data observability (real-time oversight, anomaly detection, pipeline visualization, alerting), and fostering continuous improvement through iterative testing and feedback. top_posts.title: What is Context Engineering?
top_posts.summary: Context Engineering is the practice of designing and operationalizing business meaning, data lineage, quality signals, and policy constraints so AI systems can reliably understand and act on enterprise data. Unlike prompt engineering (which focuses on how questions are asked), Context Engineering establishes what AI systems know before questions are posed. It comprises four core components: semantic context (business definitions), lineage context (data flow and dependencies), operational context (quality and reliability signals), and policy context (compliance and usage constraints). This foundation is critical for Agentic AI systems that reason and act autonomously, enabling them to assess risk correctly, explain decisions, and know when to escalate. Enterprises should prepare by inventorying critical data, unifying metadata into a single context layer, and exposing context through APIs for AI agent consumption.
